BUILD:
1. rewrite-<relation> (four relations, FK order). Preconditions: authenticated plan + sealed archetype-empty proof; relation logically empty (both target counts zero); no open BATCH_STARTED for it; the autovacuum fence for this relation open (adopt it) or, if aborted earlier, re-establish it through 016 first with the age/ceiling checks exactly as a delete does; no different relation's fence open; writer fence enabled (option b) and verified; host purge lease and pgBackRest schedule lock held for the whole life; tablespace/WAL placement and installed-wrapper hash re-checked; pre-start floor: the plan's rehearsal-based projected rewrite peak x 1.5 must leave >= 100 GB free (refuse with rewrite_peak_not_measured if the plan has no rehearsal figure for this relation -- do not invent one; P2d supplies it). Then exactly the three steps: (1) committed REWRITE_STARTED via 016 recording relation OID, relfilenode and sizes, backend PID and backend_start; (2) fixed VACUUM (FULL, ANALYZE) v3_derived.<allowlisted table via closed case mapping> on its own, under SET ROLE v3_derived_purge_executor, short lock_timeout and a per-relation statement_timeout taken from the plan (refuse if absent); (3) verify (relfilenode changed, last_analyze later than REWRITE_STARTED, published count unchanged, FK/index/trigger validity, pointers unchanged, sizes) and append REWRITE_VERIFIED, which restores the autovacuum fence through 016; on a verification failure against a CHANGED relfilenode append FAILED_STOP with rewrite_committed true and integrity_failed true and leave the writer fence closed.
2. The rewrite monitor (design 4.2 'The 100 GB floor is enforced during a rewrite'): started before step 2 as a transient root-owned systemd-run unit pinned to the container and the recorded PID + backend_start; its lifetime is the backend's (exits when pg_stat_activity no longer shows it). Polls at a short fixed interval: data-filesystem free bytes vs the floor, pg_wal size, replication-slot health and BOTH archiver tests (failed_count snapshot at start must not rise; last_failed_time not newer than last_archived_time); and whether the wrapper/controller process that started it is still alive. On any breach or controller loss it calls v3_meta.cancel_purge_rewrite (and nothing else) and appends REWRITE_CANCEL_REQUESTED naming the condition. Read-only otherwise; holds no lease; never signals any other backend. Keep its code small and in the hashed script identity.
3. Re-dispatch resolution: a rewrite-<relation> dispatch that finds an open REWRITE_STARTED first checks no VACUUM FULL/ANALYZE of that relation is running (pg_stat_progress_cluster / _analyze), then compares relfilenode with the recorded value: changed -> run ANALYZE v3_derived.<table>, verify last_analyze > REWRITE_STARTED time, then step-3 verification and REWRITE_VERIFIED with recovered:true (or FAILED_STOP with rewrite_committed/integrity_failed on failure); unchanged -> REWRITE_ROLLED_BACK, then the rewrite may run normally under a fresh REWRITE_STARTED. Never rewrite twice when relfilenode changed.
4. Trap and restore-services rewrite branches: on interruption during a rewrite, cancel the recorded backend through cancel_purge_rewrite, wait until it is gone and neither progress view shows the relation, then resolve exactly as item 3 before restoring the writer fence; never restore after integrity_failed. restore-services resolves an open REWRITE_STARTED the same way (replacing the current refusal).
5. Migration 016 amendment (016 is NOT applied in production; it may be edited, exactly as PR #817 did): let the owner-acknowledged writer-fence restore record the acknowledgement durably. Add to 016 the minimal change so the writer-fence restore path (purge_set_writer_fence / its restore and verify functions, whichever 016 uses to append WRITER_FENCE_RESTORED) accepts an optional acknowledge_failed_stop event sequence that must name an existing FAILED_STOP with integrity_failed=true for the same plan, and records it in the WRITER_FENCE_RESTORED payload. Do not otherwise weaken 016. Then wire restore-services --acknowledge-failed-stop=<sequence> to it (replacing integrity_failed_stop_acknowledgement_payload_unsupported_016). The P2a fence keeps refusing other mutators on the integrity FAILED_STOP (separate repair authority) -- keep that and say so in the runbook. Regenerate sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt, deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json (to_migration_set_identity, schema_identity_sha256, checksums in the evidence text) and the pinned values in tests/test_v3_system_search_production_operator.py with scripts/operator/v3_schema_identity.py; update the release-gate and lineage tests as #817 did. Add PG18 tests for the acknowledgement path (accepted only for a matching integrity FAILED_STOP; refused otherwise).
6. Flaky test: tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py::test_verified_rewrite_retries_do_not_open_rewrite_or_autovacuum_fence[non_superuser] intermittently fails in CI with 'competing writing transaction' raised from v3_meta.purge_assert_phase (it passed on rerun). Find which backend holds a transaction ID at that moment (a fixture connection left in a transaction, a test-local helper, or a background worker) and make the test deterministic without weakening 016's check (for example close/commit the leftover connection, or reuse the bounded wait already used by the fixtures). Audit the other purge PG18 tests for the same pattern.
7. Tests: operator contract and PG18 tests for: the three steps and their ledger rows; refusal without rehearsal figures; monitor cancels on a floor breach with its parent alive, on each archiver condition, and on controller loss, and exits when the backend is gone, never signalling another backend; re-dispatch after a committed rewrite does not rewrite twice and runs the recovered ANALYZE; re-dispatch after a rolled-back rewrite rewrites normally; trap/restore-services resolve an open rewrite before restoring; complete now works end-to-end on a disposable database once every relation is rewritten. Keep new PG18 tests small; the Finder PG18 lane has a 45-minute pytest bound and already takes ~34 minutes -- if your additions risk it, put the heavier rewrite tests in a separate new PG18 test module and say so.
